question: What integer-rounded percentage of the total length of the harlequin shrimp recorded in Omar Valencfia-Mendez 2017 paper was the sea star fed to the same type of shrimp in G. Curt Fiedler's 2002 paper?

history.name: user
history.content: What integer-rounded percentage of the total length of the harlequin shrimp recorded in Omar Valencfia-Mendez 2017 paper was the sea star fed to the same type of shrimp in G. Curt Fiedler's 2002 paper?

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content:
Task: Compute integer-rounded percentage = (sea star size fed in Fiedler 2002) / (harlequin shrimp total length reported by Omar Valencfia-Mendez 2017) × 100.
Agents: Assistant (planning/calculation), WebSurfer (web search), FileSurfer (file extraction).
Plan:
- Get exact total length of harlequin shrimp from Omar Valencfia-Mendez 2017.
- Find the sea star size fed to harlequin shrimp in Fiedler 2002 (Methods/Results).
- Ensure units are consistent, then compute and round to the nearest integer.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Search suggestions:
- For 2017 paper: "Omar Valencia-Méndez 2017 harlequin shrimp total length Journal of Threatened Taxa PDF"
- For 2002 paper: "Fiedler 2002 Hymenocera picta Linckia multifora arm fragment size cm methods"

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Search: Omar Valencia-Méndez 2017 harlequin shrimp total length.
Result: Journal of Threatened Taxa short communication by Omar Valencia-Méndez et al. (2017) on Harlequin Shrimp record in the southern Mexican Pacific. Visible snippet indicates measurements include total length in millimeters; one specimen noted at 49 mm TL. Opening details shows: “Total length (TL) 49 mm” reported for one individual.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Confirm the exact wording and unit conversion. Capture the line for the total length and convert to centimeters. FileSurfer, if a PDF is accessible, extract the exact TL figure.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Opened the Journal of Threatened Taxa item; in the measurement section, a line states: “Total length (TL) 49 mm.” Another specimen is slightly smaller but the explicit TL given 49 mm is clear. No apparent ambiguity in units (mm).

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: No local file available. From the visible snippet and page text: Recorded total length (TL) = 49 mm in Omar Valencia-Méndez et al. 2017. Saving TL=49 mm as the shrimp length datum.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Shrimp total length confirmed: 49 mm = 4.9 cm. Storing TL_shrimp = 49 mm.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Next: Find in Fiedler (2002) the size of the sea star fed to harlequin shrimp. Look for Methods text specifying prey size (e.g., arm segment length, diameter), preferably in cm or mm.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Search: Fiedler 2002 Hymenocera picta Linckia multifora arm segment mm.
Found a master's thesis referencing Fiedler: “Following Fiedler (2002), shrimp were offered Linckia multifora arm segments measuring 9–12 mm in length.” The thesis cites the Journal of Crustacean Biology paper (Vol. 22 Issue 4).

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Good. Cross-check with a second independent source to reduce risk of propagation error. Prefer peer-reviewed or conference sources that replicate Fiedler’s protocol.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Found a conference poster on harlequin shrimp feeding protocol: “Replicating Fiedler (2002), we used L. multifora arm pieces at approximately 1 cm (±2 mm).” Although not peer reviewed, it aligns with the 9–12 mm range.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Clarify measurement definition: Are these lengths linear arm segment lengths (not diameter)? Also, any more authoritative text (methods or a handbook) corroborating the fragment size?

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Located an aquarium husbandry guide referencing Fiedler (2002): “Offer Linckia multifora arm tips ~1 cm to harlequin shrimp, renewing as needed.” It appears to refer to linear fragment length rather than diameter. No direct quote from the journal methods is visible.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Caution: These sources describe fragments rather than whole sea stars. The question asks for “the sea star fed,” but Fiedler’s protocol uses arm fragments. If the 2002 study did not feed whole stars, the fragment length reflects the prey item. Suggest using midpoint of the 9–12 mm range: 10.5 mm, but recommend verifying if Fiedler ever specifies an exact size or a range formally in the Methods.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Acknowledged. Given the repeated references aligning on ~1 cm arm segments, proceed with 10.5 mm as the representative sea star piece length. We'll treat the prey as the arm segment delivered, since that’s what Fiedler fed. Compute using TL_shrimp = 49 mm.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Additional corroboration: A lab exercise handout states: “Provide harlequin shrimp with L. multifora arm fragments of approximately 1 cm length (following Fiedler 2002).” Arm width noted around 3 mm, but that’s not relevant to our length calculation.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Compute percentage: sea star fragment length 10.5 mm; shrimp total length 49 mm.
Ratio = 10.5 / 49 = 0.2142857 → 21.42857%.
Integer-rounded (nearest) = 21%.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Confirm rounding convention: nearest integer. Assistant has computed 21% based on midpoint of the cited range. Before finalizing, note we did not directly verify Fiedler’s primary Methods text; we are relying on secondary references. Time check: proceed?
